brief: Goldman's Prime Services weekly covers 9/25-10/1. The Fundamental L/S performance estimate fell 0.45% (vs MSCI World -0.67%), driven almost entirely by beta as alpha finished flat; the Systematic L/S estimate rose 1.14%, driven by alpha of 1.27% from short-side gains, partly offset by -0.13% beta. Overall book gross leverage held at 308.0% and net leverage at 77.4%, both unchanged, but the Fundamental L/S sub-book delevered: gross down 1.7 points to 206.2% (21st percentile) and net down 2.1 points to 53.0% (7th percentile). Equities were net bought overall (+0.7 SDs), long buys outpacing short sales 2.7-to-1, led by Europe and North America. Macro Products saw net buying at the fastest pace in two months, driven by short covers, while Single Stocks were net sold for a third straight week, driven by short sales. Health Care led buying, its largest percentage net-buy in over six months on short covers and long buys; Info Tech led selling, its largest percentage net-sell in six weeks on long sales in EM Asia and Europe. Regionally, Europe drove the week's biggest flow swing via long buys and short covers; by sector, Utilities drove buying and Real Estate drove selling.
